entities.summary:
Bryson of Heraclea was an ancient Greek mathematician and sophist who studied the solving the problems of squaring the circle and calculating pi. Born in Heraclea Pontica, a city in ancient Greece, Bryson was trained in the arts of rhetoric and gymnastics, which he applied to his mathematical pursuits. His work on the Apollonian circle and the calculation of pi were highly influential, and he was often invited to speak at intellectual salons in Athens and other Greek cities.

As a sophist, Bryson was known for his eloquence and his ability to adapt his arguments to suit his audience. His mathematical work, however, was marked by a rigorous attention to detail and a willingness to challenge established theories. Bryson's legacy extends beyond his own time, as his work on the Apollonian circle influenced later mathematicians such as Archimedes and Euclid.

Despite his significant contributions to mathematics, Bryson's personal life remains somewhat of a mystery. He was known to have been a member of the Athenian assembly and was involved in various intellectual and cultural pursuits, but little is known about his family or his later life.

Bryson's mathematical achievements have left a lasting impact on our understanding of the circle and its properties. His work on the Apollonian circle has been widely studied and built upon, and his contributions to the development of geometry and trigonometry continue to be celebrated by mathematicians today.
